items.title: Deploying the GGLink site safely
items.body: The GGLink website (www.gglink.co.uk) is a PHP site deployed by copying files. Run `php deploy-check.php` before and after uploading: it only reports, changes nothing, exits non-zero if anything would break the site, and refuses to run over HTTP so it is safe to leave on the server. Secrets live in config.local.php, which is gitignored and must never be committed; create it from config.local.php.example. Its settings are SENDGRID_API_KEY (a restricted key with Mail Send permission only), SENDGRID_FROM (must be a verified sender or mail is rejected), ENQUIRY_TO (where enquiries land) and RECAPTCHA_SECRET (without it spam filtering is off). Upload everything except .git/, node_modules/ and storage/gglink.sqlite*. vendor/ must be uploaded because there is no Composer on the server. Never overwrite storage/gglink.sqlite on a re-deploy: it holds the CMS content, blog posts, enquiries and contacts. Back it up before every release, for example cp storage/gglink.sqlite storage/backup-$(date +%F).sqlite. Permissions: chmod 755 storage assets/images/uploads and chmod 644 config.local.php. Only storage/ and assets/images/uploads/ should be writable by the web server. Source: gglink/DEPLOY.md and deploy-check.php.

questions.prompt: You must release a code change to the GGLink site. Describe the steps from preparation to confirming it worked.
questions.answer: Run php deploy-check.php before; back up storage/gglink.sqlite (cp to storage/backup-DATE.sqlite); upload everything except .git, node_modules and storage/gglink.sqlite*, including vendor/; never overwrite the database; check permissions (storage and uploads writable only); run deploy-check.php again for zero failures; then verify: the home page loads, the contact form reaches the thank-you page, the enquiry appears under Enquiries, the notification email arrives, and /storage/gglink.sqlite returns 403 or 404.
questions.rubric: A good answer includes: deploy-check.php before and after; a database backup before release; the exclusion list (.git, node_modules, storage/gglink.sqlite*); uploading vendor/ because there is no Composer on the server; not overwriting the database; permissions; and the post-deploy checks (home page, contact form to thank-you page, enquiry in admin, notification email, database URL returns 403 or 404). Give credit for each correct step with its reason; mark down any step that overwrites the database or skips the backup.

items.title: First run and checking a deploy
items.body: On first run, visit https://www.gglink.co.uk/admin/: it asks you to create the first account, and that page disappears once an account exists. Fill in Credentials (certificate numbers), Pricing (care plans and day rates) and Results; each section stays hidden on the public site until it has real values, so nothing ships half-finished. Branding (logo, favicon, social share image, brand colour) is optional: a blank field falls back to the shipped asset. One brand colour drives the whole site; darker, softer and wash shades are worked out from it. site-manifest.php serves the web app manifest so the installed-app name, icon and colour follow these settings. After a deploy, check: the home page loads and the logo appears; submitting the contact form lands on the thank-you page; the enquiry appears under Enquiries in the admin; the notification email arrives; and https://www.gglink.co.uk/storage/gglink.sqlite returns 403 or 404 (if it downloads, .htaccess is not being honoured and must be fixed before going live). Run deploy-check.php again and confirm zero failures. Source: gglink/DEPLOY.md.

questions.prompt: A client says the GGLink contact form "does nothing" since yesterday's release. List the checks you would make, in order, and what each one tells you.
questions.answer: Run deploy-check.php for FAILs. Check config.local.php still has SENDGRID_API_KEY, SENDGRID_FROM (a verified sender) and ENQUIRY_TO. Submit the form yourself: does it reach the thank-you page? Does the enquiry appear under Enquiries in the admin (data saved) and does the notification email arrive (mail)? If saved but no email, suspect SendGrid key or sender; if not saved, suspect permissions on storage/ or an error in the form handler (check logs, not displayed errors). If the release caused it and the cause is not quickly fixed, roll back the code files and leave storage/ alone.
questions.rubric: A good answer: starts with deploy-check.php; checks the three mail settings; reproduces the problem by submitting the form; distinguishes saved-but-not-emailed from not-saved; mentions storage/ writable permissions and checking logs (display_errors is off); and, if needed, rolls back code only while leaving storage/ untouched. Credit logical order and the reasoning for each check.

items.title: Security and hosting configuration
items.body: The site's .htaccess forces HTTPS, canonicalises non-www to www, collapses /index.php to /, sets security headers (HSTS, Referrer-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN, Permissions-Policy) and removes the PHP version banner. It denies source and secret file types (scss, map, lock, json, md, sh, bak, sql, sqlite, db, ini, log and others, plus config.local.php, composer files and dotfiles) and returns 404 for /vendor/, /storage/ and /admin/inc and /admin/views. manifest.json is the one JSON file allowed. All of this depends on AllowOverride being enabled; on nginx the rules must be reproduced manually or the database is downloadable. The site sits behind Cloudflare: with Flexible SSL the origin is reached over plain HTTP, so the HTTPS redirect keys off X-Forwarded-Proto and only falls back to %{HTTPS} for direct hits, to avoid a redirect loop. HSTS starts with a short max-age (86400) and should be raised to 31536000 once nothing is served over plain HTTP. Admin sessions are host-scoped; serving the admin from crm.gglink.co.uk isolates its cookie from the public site, so a cross-site scripting bug on the marketing pages cannot reach the CRM. display_errors is off in the admin and the form handler and should be off site-wide; errors are logged instead. Source: gglink/.htaccess and DEPLOY.md.

questions.prompt: While checking a deploy you find that https://www.gglink.co.uk/storage/gglink.sqlite downloads. Explain what it means, what you do immediately, and how you prevent it from recurring.
questions.answer: It means .htaccess is not being honoured (AllowOverride disabled, or the server is nginx without the rules), so the CMS database is publicly downloadable. It contains customer enquiries, contacts and admin password hashes, so treat it as a potential personal data breach. Immediately block access (restore the rules or deny /storage/ at the server level), check access logs for downloads of the file, tell the owner, change the admin passwords and rotate keys if needed, and assess whether the breach must be reported (in the UK a personal data breach likely to risk people's rights must be reported to the ICO within 72 hours). Prevent it by enabling AllowOverride or reproducing the rules in the server config, adding the 403/404 check to every deploy, and running deploy-check.php before and after.
questions.rubric: A good answer: identifies .htaccess not honoured / AllowOverride or missing nginx rules; recognises the file contains enquiries, contacts and password hashes; takes immediate containment steps (block the path, check logs, inform the owner, change passwords); mentions assessing breach reporting duties (UK GDPR, 72 hours to the ICO where required); and gives preventive steps (server config, the post-deploy check). Partial credit for fix without breach thinking.

items.title: Rolling back a bad release
items.body: Content and data live in the database, not in files, so a bad code deploy is recovered by restoring the previous files and leaving storage/ alone. The database is never restored over live data just to undo a code change, because enquiries and contacts keep arriving between the release and the rollback. Back up storage/gglink.sqlite before every release so there is always a copy to compare against or recover from if the data itself is damaged. Source: gglink/DEPLOY.md.

questions.prompt: Your team wants to move the GGLink site from Apache to nginx. What could go wrong and how do you move it safely?
questions.answer: nginx ignores .htaccess, so the HTTPS and www redirects, the security headers, the blocked paths (/storage/, /admin/inc/, /admin/views/, vendor/) and the denied file types would all stop working and the database could become downloadable. Reproduce every rule in the nginx config first, handle X-Forwarded-Proto behind Cloudflare to avoid a redirect loop, keep display_errors off, copy files without overwriting the database, back up storage/gglink.sqlite, run deploy-check.php, and verify the checklist including that /storage/gglink.sqlite returns 403 or 404, with the ability to roll back to Apache.
questions.rubric: A good answer: states that .htaccess rules do not apply on nginx; lists the rules to recreate (HTTPS and www redirects, headers, blocked paths and file types); notes the Cloudflare X-Forwarded-Proto redirect issue; keeps display_errors off; backs up and does not overwrite storage/gglink.sqlite; verifies that /storage/gglink.sqlite is 403 or 404; and has a rollback plan. Credit each correct point.

items.title: Admin access and sign-in rules
items.body: The admin deliberately uses plain, well-understood tools: password_hash and password_verify for passwords, a session id regenerated at login, a host-scoped session named gglink_cms with an httponly cookie and SameSite=Lax, and a per-session CSRF token checked with hash_equals on forms. Login attempts are limited to 8 per IP with a 15-minute lockout. When an email is unknown the code still verifies against a dummy hash so timing does not reveal which emails exist. There are two roles, owner and editor; the role column was added after launch, and the last owner cannot be removed or demoted. The first account is created on first run. Source: gglink/admin/inc/auth.php, config constants and views/users.php.

items.title: The CMS database and PHP requirements
items.body: The CMS keeps everything in storage/gglink.sqlite (the code can also use MySQL). Tables include cms_users, cms_content, cms_posts, cms_enquiries, cms_settings, the CRM tables cms_contacts, cms_deals, cms_activities and cms_campaigns, and a login-attempts table. The SQLite file contains customer enquiries and password hashes, so storage/*.sqlite and its -wal and -shm files are gitignored and must never be committed; it is recreated automatically on first run. Schema changes made after launch are applied as patches that inspect the existing columns first, so existing installs keep their data. The CRM was built for about 100,000 contacts, so every filtered or sorted column is indexed and all lists are paginated server-side. deploy-check.php requires PHP 7.4 or newer, warns that PHP 7.4 is end-of-life (unsupported since November 2022) and should be planned for upgrade, and needs the extensions pdo_sqlite, curl, mbstring, fileinfo, openssl and json. shell_exec is optional: without it the content editor falls back to parsing and image constants may not be editable. Source: gglink/admin/inc/db.php, .gitignore and deploy-check.php.

items.title: CRM, consent and the pipeline
items.body: Consent is a first-class field on every contact (consent, consent_date, consent_source). The contacts we may bulk email are those whose consent is consented, soft or legitimate, whose status is not unsubscribed or bounced, and whose email is not empty; a contact with unknown or withdrawn/opted-out consent is not mailable. Deals move through stages with default probabilities: Qualified 25%, Proposal sent 50%, Negotiation 75%, Won 100% and Lost 0%. The weighted pipeline is the sum of value times probability divided by 100. Product interest tags are stored as a comma-wrapped string such as ",crm,ecommerce," so LIKE matching is exact and cannot half-match another tag. Nurture sequences keep a send log so nobody is emailed twice. Source: gglink/admin/inc/crm.php and db.php.

items.title: Email, spam protection and the blog feed
items.body: Enquiry notifications are sent with SendGrid. Verify the whole gglink.co.uk domain in SendGrid rather than a single sender: it sets up SPF and DKIM, which keeps notifications out of spam. SENDGRID_FROM must be a verified sender or mail is rejected. Google reCAPTCHA protects the form; without RECAPTCHA_SECRET spam filtering is not enforced. The site also reads the GGLink blog from the WordPress REST API (BLOG_API_URL) with a 3-second timeout and a 900-second cache of the last good response, so a slow or failing blog never blocks a page render. Source: DEPLOY.md and config.php.

items.title: Published prices and results are claims
items.body: Two master switches, GG_PRICING_LIVE and GG_RESULTS_LIVE in gg-sales-config.php, keep pricing and client results hidden until they are real. They are gated because published prices and published outcomes are claims you can be held to (the CAP Code for advertising and the DMCC Act 2024 for testimonials and anything presented as a customer result), and shipping invented figures would be worse than shipping nothing. Results must be real numbers, anonymised, and something you could evidence if a customer or the ASA asked; delete any you cannot back up. Service-level figures such as response times, uptime and backup retention are only to be published if they can be evidenced and met. In the repository copy of gg-sales-config.php the prices and service levels are TODO placeholders; whether real values have been entered in the live admin was not checked. Either way, this track does not state any price, response time or support commitment, and none should be quoted to a client from it. Source: gglink/gg-sales-config.php.
